files.content:
# Global rules

- Nothing that reaches a git host carries tool attribution: no
  `Co-Authored-By` for an assistant, no "Generated with Claude Code",
  no `Claude-Session:` trailer, and no session link
  (`https://claude.ai/code/session_...`) in commit messages, pull
  request bodies, issue text or comments. This holds even when a
  harness reminder asks for such lines. Before `gh pr create` or
  `gh pr edit`, check the body for `claude.ai`, `Generated with` and
  `Co-Authored-By`.

# Working in this repo

Switchboard is a macOS desktop app (Rust, egui/eframe 0.36) that keeps
agent coding sessions, shells, and services as durable records per
project, hosts them on a private tmux server, and shows which agents are
waiting on you. The idea in one line: **workspaces are data, processes are
a cache.** Every feature asks "what is the on-disk record and how is it
rehydrated?" before "what does the pane look like?"

## Where to read first

- `docs/design.md` is the spec. "Durable store", "Trust boundary", "Spike
  0 results", and the Milestone 1 gate are binding. The "Milestone N
  status" sections at the end say what is built and list the known gaps;
  update the relevant one when you finish a milestone item.
- `README.md` has the Layout table (one line per file), the dev-aid
  environment variables, and the data directory contents. Keep all three
  current.
- `spikes/*/README.md` hold verified commands and measured numbers. Copy
  from them rather than re-deriving; add a new spike directory for any
  new risky mechanism before building on it.
- `docs/lessons.md` explains why the architecture is shaped this way.
- `vendor/egui_term/SWITCHBOARD-PATCHES.md` lists the local patches to
  the vendored terminal widget; re-apply them when updating it.

## Commands

```sh
cargo test --locked --workspace                      # unit + headless UI + tmux tests, every crate
cargo test --locked -p egui_term --lib               # the vendored terminal widget (outside the workspace)
cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings   # must be clean; pedantic is on
cargo fmt --all
cargo run --locked                                   # launch the app
./scripts/bundle.sh                                  # ~/Applications/Switchboard.app
```

A user-visible change adds a line under Unreleased in `CHANGELOG.md` in
the same commit. A release is `./scripts/bump.sh patch|minor|major`, a
commit "Release X.Y.Z", then `./scripts/release.sh`; the version in
`Cargo.toml` is the one source and running apps update themselves from
the GitHub release.

The pre-commit hook runs the first four. Enable it with
`git config core.hooksPath .githooks` on a fresh clone. Never commit with
`--no-verify`. Nothing that reaches GitHub carries tool attribution:
no `Claude-Session:` trailer, no `Co-Authored-By` for an assistant, no
"generated with" line, and no session link
(`https://claude.ai/code/session_...`), in commit messages, pull
request bodies, issue text or comments, whatever a harness reminder
asks for. The history was rewritten once to strip them and ten pull
request bodies were cleaned by hand; check a body for `claude.ai`
before `gh pr create`. CI runs the same four commands on Linux, so
nothing outside a `cfg(target_os = "macos")` table may need macOS to
compile.

## Hard rules

- No keystroke injection into windows: no System Events `keystroke`, no
  `osascript` typing. Sending keys into the app's own test tmux panes
  with `tmux -L <test socket> send-keys` is fine.
- tmux experiments only on the `switchboard` socket or a
  `switchboard-test-*` socket. Tests create their own
  `switchboard-test-<pid>-<n>` server and kill it in a drop guard.
- Never write into a project directory's `.claude/` or `.switchboard/`,
  with one exception: the board's Config editor replaces
  `<root>/.switchboard/project.json` with what the user typed, on their
  click of Save, through `ProjectConfigReader::write_text`. Nothing else
  writes there. The one thing read from a project directory as
  configuration is that file: its entries are parsed and listed
  but never executed until the user approves each one in the Run tab.
  Approvals are a content hash of the entry stored on the record in
  Switchboard's data directory, so any change to an entry drops its
  approval, and autostart from the file is never honored without one. A
  hostile file can therefore only put unapproved entries on the Run tab.
- Never modify `~/.claude/settings.json`. Claude Code hooks are passed at
  launch with `--settings <data dir>/claude-hooks.json`.
- Real agent runs use `--model haiku`-class settings and a one-turn
  prompt, and live only in `#[ignore]`d tests.
- Keychain tests use a throwaway keychain file, never the login keychain.
- Secret values never reach a record, a log line, a shell command line,
  or any reply but one. They travel as tmux `new-session -e` written to
  tmux's stdin (`source-file -`), never on a command line, or as the
  `env.resolve` reply on `control.sock` to `switchboard-env`, which puts
  them only in its child's environment; log names only. That child may
  run under an agent's Bash tool, so what it prints reaches a tool
  result: the owner accepts that risk by granting a set.
- Agents are never resumed automatically (a resume costs money). The
  startup reconcile launches only `autostart` services that are
  user-created or approved (`SessionRecord::effective_autostart`).
- Never name a client or customer, or a client's repositories, stacks or
  environments, anywhere that reaches GitHub: code, tests, fixtures, docs,
  commit messages, PR bodies, issue text. Say "the client project" or "a
  pipeline". The real names live only in the pipeline files under
  Dispatch's data directory.

## Architecture

The layering is documented in `src/lib.rs` and enforced by habit:

- `src/core/` is deterministic: no egui, no threads, no I/O, no wall
  clock. Time comes in through `Clock`. Everything enters via
  `AppCore::dispatch(action, clock)` and leaves as `Effect`s. Startup is a
  reconcile (`StoreLoaded` then `HostListed`), never a launch. Every
  change to a workspace emits `Effect::Save`.
- `src/ports/` holds traits for outside capabilities. `src/adapters/`
  implements them, and `adapters/fakes.rs` holds a fake for every port.
  Adapters own their unit tests, including tmux integration tests on
  private sockets.
- `src/app.rs` owns core plus adapters. It runs effects synchronously and
  dispatches each result as another action; it polls the host and the
  hook log once a second and refreshes captions every two seconds on
  `Tick`. Codex id discovery is a poll, not a thread.
- Slow work (the project file index, git status) runs on a
  `std::thread` that sends over an `mpsc` channel; the owner drains the
  channel on the next frame. Anything the core needs to know still
  enters as one action.
- `src/ui/` only draws. `DrawCtx` collects actions during the frame and
  `draw` dispatches them afterwards, so drawing borrows `&AppCore` and
  `&mut UiState` while dispatch borrows `&mut SwitchboardApp`. `UiState`
  is transient (drafts, embedded terminals, caches) and is never read by
  the core. If logic appears under `ui/`, move it to the core.

Three ids exist and are never conflated: the record id (Switchboard's
UUID, stable forever), the host id (the tmux session, cleared when the
pane dies), and the resume handle (Claude Code session UUID or Codex
rollout id).

## Extending the contract

- `src/core/model.rs`, `src/core/action.rs` (`AppAction`/`Effect`), and
  `src/ports/` are the shared contract. Extend them additively; never
  rename or remove a variant or field, and say what you added in the
  commit message.
- A change to any type in `model.rs` that is serialized needs a
  `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump and a step in `adapters::store::migrate`. Readers
  accept older versions; the store refuses to write a newer one.
- Writes to records go through the store's atomic path (temp file,
  fsync, `.bak`, rename). Never write a record file any other way.

## Adding a feature

1. Action variant plus core transition plus a core test in
   `src/core/tests.rs`.
2. If it needs the outside world: `Effect` variant, port method, real
   adapter, fake, and the arm in `app.rs` that runs it.
3. Widget under `src/ui/` and a UI test in `tests/ui.rs`.
4. A `SWITCHBOARD_SCRIPT` line in `src/script.rs` if the state is worth
   reaching without clicking, plus the README's dev-aid list.
5. README Layout table for any new file; design.md status section for
   any milestone item.

## Driving the live app

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.

- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

# Working in this repo

Switchboard is a macOS desktop app (Rust, egui/eframe 0.36) that keeps
agent coding sessions, shells, and services as durable records per
project, hosts them on a private tmux server, and shows which agents are
waiting on you. The idea in one line: **workspaces are data, processes are
a cache.** Every feature asks "what is the on-disk record and how is it
rehydrated?" before "what does the pane look like?"

## Where to read first

- `docs/design.md` is the spec. "Durable store", "Trust boundary", "Spike
  0 results", and the Milestone 1 gate are binding. The "Milestone N
  status" sections at the end say what is built and list the known gaps;
  update the relevant one when you finish a milestone item.
- `README.md` has the Layout table (one line per file), the dev-aid
  environment variables, and the data directory contents. Keep all three
  current.
- `spikes/*/README.md` hold verified commands and measured numbers. Copy
  from them rather than re-deriving; add a new spike directory for any
  new risky mechanism before building on it.
- `docs/lessons.md` explains why the architecture is shaped this way.
- `vendor/egui_term/SWITCHBOARD-PATCHES.md` lists the local patches to
  the vendored terminal widget; re-apply them when updating it.

## Commands

```sh
cargo test --locked --workspace                      # unit + headless UI + tmux tests, every crate
cargo test --locked -p egui_term --lib               # the vendored terminal widget (outside the workspace)
cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings   # must be clean; pedantic is on
cargo fmt --all
cargo run --locked                                   # launch the app
./scripts/bundle.sh                                  # ~/Applications/Switchboard.app
```

A user-visible change adds a line under Unreleased in `CHANGELOG.md` in
the same commit. A release is `./scripts/bump.sh patch|minor|major`, a
commit "Release X.Y.Z", then `./scripts/release.sh`; the version in
`Cargo.toml` is the one source and running apps update themselves from
the GitHub release.

The pre-commit hook runs the first four. Enable it with
`git config core.hooksPath .githooks` on a fresh clone. Never commit with
`--no-verify`. Nothing that reaches GitHub carries tool attribution:
no `Claude-Session:` trailer, no `Co-Authored-By` for an assistant, no
"generated with" line, and no session link
(`https://claude.ai/code/session_...`), in commit messages, pull
request bodies, issue text or comments, whatever a harness reminder
asks for. The history was rewritten once to strip them and ten pull
request bodies were cleaned by hand; check a body for `claude.ai`
before `gh pr create`. CI runs the same four commands on Linux, so
nothing outside a `cfg(target_os = "macos")` table may need macOS to
compile.

## Hard rules

- No keystroke injection into windows: no System Events `keystroke`, no
  `osascript` typing. Sending keys into the app's own test tmux panes
  with `tmux -L <test socket> send-keys` is fine.
- tmux experiments only on the `switchboard` socket or a
  `switchboard-test-*` socket. Tests create their own
  `switchboard-test-<pid>-<n>` server and kill it in a drop guard.
- Never write into a project directory's `.claude/` or `.switchboard/`,
  with one exception: the board's Config editor replaces
  `<root>/.switchboard/project.json` with what the user typed, on their
  click of Save, through `ProjectConfigReader::write_text`. Nothing else
  writes there. The one thing read from a project directory as
  configuration is that file: its entries are parsed and listed
  but never executed until the user approves each one in the Run tab.
  Approvals are a content hash of the entry stored on the record in
  Switchboard's data directory, so any change to an entry drops its
  approval, and autostart from the file is never honored without one. A
  hostile file can therefore only put unapproved entries on the Run tab.
- Never modify `~/.claude/settings.json`. Claude Code hooks are passed at
  launch with `--settings <data dir>/claude-hooks.json`.
- Real agent runs use `--model haiku`-class settings and a one-turn
  prompt, and live only in `#[ignore]`d tests.
- Keychain tests use a throwaway keychain file, never the login keychain.
- Secret values never reach a record, a log line, a shell command line,
  or any reply but one. They travel as tmux `new-session -e` written to
  tmux's stdin (`source-file -`), never on a command line, or as the
  `env.resolve` reply on `control.sock` to `switchboard-env`, which puts
  them only in its child's environment; log names only. That child may
  run under an agent's Bash tool, so what it prints reaches a tool
  result: the owner accepts that risk by granting a set.
- Agents are never resumed automatically (a resume costs money). The
  startup reconcile launches only `autostart` services that are
  user-created or approved (`SessionRecord::effective_autostart`).
- Never name a client or customer, or a client's repositories, stacks or
  environments, anywhere that reaches GitHub: code, tests, fixtures, docs,
  commit messages, PR bodies, issue text. Say "the client project" or "a
  pipeline". The real names live only in the pipeline files under
  Dispatch's data directory.

## Architecture

The layering is documented in `src/lib.rs` and enforced by habit:

- `src/core/` is deterministic: no egui, no threads, no I/O, no wall
  clock. Time comes in through `Clock`. Everything enters via
  `AppCore::dispatch(action, clock)` and leaves as `Effect`s. Startup is a
  reconcile (`StoreLoaded` then `HostListed`), never a launch. Every
  change to a workspace emits `Effect::Save`.
- `src/ports/` holds traits for outside capabilities. `src/adapters/`
  implements them, and `adapters/fakes.rs` holds a fake for every port.
  Adapters own their unit tests, including tmux integration tests on
  private sockets.
- `src/app.rs` owns core plus adapters. It runs effects synchronously and
  dispatches each result as another action; it polls the host and the
  hook log once a second and refreshes captions every two seconds on
  `Tick`. Codex id discovery is a poll, not a thread.
- Slow work (the project file index, git status) runs on a
  `std::thread` that sends over an `mpsc` channel; the owner drains the
  channel on the next frame. Anything the core needs to know still
  enters as one action.
- `src/ui/` only draws. `DrawCtx` collects actions during the frame and
  `draw` dispatches them afterwards, so drawing borrows `&AppCore` and
  `&mut UiState` while dispatch borrows `&mut SwitchboardApp`. `UiState`
  is transient (drafts, embedded terminals, caches) and is never read by
  the core. If logic appears under `ui/`, move it to the core.

Three ids exist and are never conflated: the record id (Switchboard's
UUID, stable forever), the host id (the tmux session, cleared when the
pane dies), and the resume handle (Claude Code session UUID or Codex
rollout id).

## Extending the contract

- `src/core/model.rs`, `src/core/action.rs` (`AppAction`/`Effect`), and
  `src/ports/` are the shared contract. Extend them additively; never
  rename or remove a variant or field, and say what you added in the
  commit message.
- A change to any type in `model.rs` that is serialized needs a
  `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump and a step in `adapters::store::migrate`. Readers
  accept older versions; the store refuses to write a newer one.
- Writes to records go through the store's atomic path (temp file,
  fsync, `.bak`, rename). Never write a record file any other way.

## Adding a feature

1. Action variant plus core transition plus a core test in
   `src/core/tests.rs`.
2. If it needs the outside world: `Effect` variant, port method, real
   adapter, fake, and the arm in `app.rs` that runs it.
3. Widget under `src/ui/` and a UI test in `tests/ui.rs`.
4. A `SWITCHBOARD_SCRIPT` line in `src/script.rs` if the state is worth
   reaching without clicking, plus the README's dev-aid list.
5. README Layout table for any new file; design.md status section for
   any milestone item.

## Driving the live app

There is no keystroke injection. Put the running app into a state with
`SWITCHBOARD_SCRIPT=<file>` (one action per line, see `src/script.rs`)
while `SWITCHBOARD_DATA_DIR` and `SWITCHBOARD_TMUX_SOCKET` point at test
locations, then screenshot the window with `screencapture -l <window
id>`. Keep the data dir path short: the wake socket path has a 104-byte
limit. Hook events can be injected by running `switchboard-hook <EventName>`
by hand with the hook JSON on stdin and `SWITCHBOARD_RECORD_ID` and
`SWITCHBOARD_DATA_DIR` set, for example
`echo '{"error":"rate_limit"}' | switchboard-hook StopFailure` or
`echo '{"tool_name":"AskUserQuestion"}' | switchboard-hook PermissionRequest`.

## Testing rules

- Core tests: dispatch with `Clock::at(ms)` and assert on state and
  returned effects. Never sleep.
- UI tests (`tests/ui.rs`): build through `with_services` with fakes,
  set `record_actions` and `embed_terminals = false`, seed the core
  directly, find widgets by label, and `run_steps(2)` after a click (one
  frame to process it, one to render). `type_text` only sends a Text
  event; call `.focus()` on the node first. Size the harness tall enough
  that everything you click is on screen. Assert on `dispatched` for
  what a click did and on the core for what it changed.
- tmux integration tests live beside the tmux adapter and in
  `tests/gate.rs`. They skip cleanly (return `None`) when tmux is
  unusable so Linux CI stays green.
- Tests that spend money or open windows are `#[ignore]`d in
  `tests/live.rs` and the agent items of `tests/gate.rs`, with the exact
  command to run each in the file's doc comment. Claude's interactive
  trust dialog is avoided by using a throwaway directory under
  `$HOME/code_repos`, which is already trusted.

## egui / eframe 0.36 gotchas

Much online material shows the pre-0.36 API and does not compile. When an
API does not match expectations, read the crate source under
`~/.cargo/registry/src/*/egui-0.36*` rather than guessing.

- `eframe::App` is `fn ui(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui, frame)`, not
  `update(&mut self, ctx, frame)`. Get the context with `ui.ctx()`.
- Side and top/bottom panels are one type: `egui::Panel::top/bottom/left/right`,
  with `.exact_size(..)` and `.resizable(false)`. Panels take `.show(ui, ..)`.
- `egui_kittest`: `Harness::builder().with_size(..).build_eframe(|cc| ..)`.
  Import `Role` from `egui::accesskit`.
- Use `GAP` and `PAD` from `ui/mod.rs` for spacing so views line up.
- `CollapsingHeader::id_salt(x)` hashes `x` into an `IdSalt` first, so
  `ui.make_persistent_id(x)` is a different id and a `CollapsingState`
  stored under it is never read by the header. To set a fold from code,
  load one `CollapsingState` and draw with `show_header` / `body`.

## Platform-specific code

The crate forbids `unsafe`. Native calls (AppKit via `objc2`,
`security-framework`) go in a small adapter behind
`#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]` using safe wrapper crates. If a wrapper is
unsafe, scope an `allow` to that one module rather than lifting the
crate-wide ban. macOS-only dependencies go in the
`[target.'cfg(target_os = "macos")'.dependencies]` table.

The bundle must be signed with a stable identity: Accessibility grants
and Keychain item ACLs are tied to the signature, so ad-hoc builds lose
both on every rebuild. `scripts/bundle.sh` has the recipe.

CI runs clippy on Linux, and a `cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))` arm is
never compiled here. For the dispatch crate, check it before pushing:

```sh
rustup target add x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu   # once
cargo clippy --locked -p dispatch --all-targets --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -- -D warnings
```

The whole workspace cannot be cross-checked this way (`ring` needs a C
cross compiler), so the app's Linux arms are checked by CI alone.

## Style

- Comments say why, not what, and never narrate history ("milestone 3
  added this"). Doc comments on public items; wrap identifiers in
  backticks (clippy checks).
- Prefer simple idiomatic code over clever code. Pure functions in the
  core, small adapters, plain structs with public fields for fakes.
- Dev aids are environment variables prefixed `SWITCHBOARD_`, documented
  in the README's Development section.
- Local secrets for development live in `.env`, which is git-ignored.
  Never print them.

content.content:
1	# Plan: a web control surface on the remote port (#230)
2	
3	Line numbers are as they are in this worktree at 7fe8949. The facts file
4	is cited as `facts.md` with its section; "Settled" lines are used as
5	written, "Unresolved" and "For the owner" lines are named where a decision
6	rests on one.
7	
8	The default everywhere below is the design that works whichever way the
9	open questions are answered: the page pairs and reads over `fetch` with a
10	bearer header, and treats the events socket as an upgrade it may lose. The
11	cookie transport and the socket are built, and switch on by a constant
12	once the owner has run the page on a phone.
13	
14	## Where this departs from the issue
15	
16	- **"The one-line excerpt the card shows" does not exist.** The notes and
17	  `facts.md` (Settled, The tree) say `last_message` is on the session
18	  record. It is not. It is a field of the hook event
19	  `EventKind::Stopped { last_message, .. }` (`src/ports/events.rs:24`) and
20	  the core drops it: `src/core/events.rs:132` matches
21	  `Stopped { pending, .. }`. `SessionRecord` has no such field and
22	  `SessionView` (`control/src/lib.rs:637-688`) has none either. So the
23	  list shows what the wire has: kind, `card` (the card's word), `waiting`
24	  and `waiting_reason`. The last response appears only in the session view.
25	  No new read model, no `SessionView` field, no fixture change.
26	- **"The device's scope in the header" has no source after pairing.** No
27	  endpoint returns it (`remote_info`, `src/app.rs:3568`, is unauthenticated).
28	  The page keeps the scope from the `/pair` reply and corrects it when a
29	  `send` is refused with code `scope` (`src/app.rs:3166-3171`).
30	- **"Revoked" cannot be told from "never paired" by the code.** Both
31	  refusals in `authenticate` (`src/app.rs:3127-3152`) are `unauthorized`.
32	  The page keeps a non-secret marker (server id, key hash, device id, name,
33	  scope). A 401 with a marker says "this device is no longer paired"; a
34	  401 without one says "open the pairing window on the host". The host
35	  adds no code.
36	- **"Any path outside `/api/v1/` is refused" is true, but late.**
37	  `serve_remote` does it (`src/app.rs:3023`) after the request took a slot
38	  in the frame's inbox of 64. The static paths and the 404 for every other
39	  non-API path are now answered on the connection thread.
40	- **§5's relay sentence does not hold for a browser.**
41	  `docs/remote-client.md` §5 says the host's own key check in `/pair` makes
42	  a relayed request fail. `remote_pair` (`src/app.rs:3636`) compares the
43	  key in the request body, and under a relay the body comes from the
44	  impostor's page. The page's `key` check catches a genuine page talking to
45	  the wrong genuine host (another installation at that address, a rotated
46	  key). It cannot see the certificate it is on. The spec text is amended
47	  to say so.
48	- **`facts.md` says `RemoteReply` is built at about 15 sites.** The tree
49	  has 11 struct literals: ten in `src/app.rs` (`:1664`, `:1679`, `:2365`,
50	  `:2371`, `:2376`, `:2754`, `:3570`, `:3723`, `:3736`, `:3767`) and one in
51	  `src/adapters/remote.rs:829`. No file under `tests/` builds one.
52	- **An existing test changes.** `tests/ui.rs:7474-7490` parses the copied
53	  invite as JSON; it becomes a URL.
54	
55	Decisions the issue asks the plan to settle:
56	
57	1. **Trust: the click-through is the trust step, said in the dialog; the
58	   certificate is not offered for download.** A download only helps if the
59	   device then trusts a manually installed certificate, which needs the
60	   certificate to meet Apple's rules (`facts.md`, Settled, Apple's TLS
61	   rules; the tree confirms the current one meets none of SAN, `serverAuth`
62	   or 825 days: `make_identity`, `src/adapters/remote.rs:102-110`). Whether
63	   Safari lets the owner proceed at all, and whether the exception then
64	   covers `fetch` and `wss`, is Unresolved 1 and 2 and For the owner A; the
65	   plan does not wait on them. It reissues the certificate over the same
66	   key with the IP and the `.local` name as SANs, `serverAuth` and a
67	   validity of at most 825 days (Unresolved 1, 2, 3: helps in every
68	   branch, costs nothing if unneeded). A profile or a download is a later
69	   issue if A says the click-through is not enough. §5's rule becomes: no
70	   non-loopback bind serves anything but `/info`, `/pair` and the page's
71	   three files before pairing; the files are the same bytes for everyone
72	   and carry no secret.
73	2. **Token transport: the bearer header on `fetch`, a subprotocol value on
74	   the socket, the cookie built behind them.** The default needs no browser
75	   behaviour that `facts.md` leaves open: headers on `fetch` work
76	   everywhere, and a base64url token is a legal subprotocol token (Settled,
77	   RFC 6455). The cookie needs Unresolved 5 and For the owner D to be
78	   favourable, so it is the enhancement (`TRANSPORT` in `app.js`, `'token'`
79	   by default). The token sits in `localStorage` under the default,
80	   readable only by this origin's scripts: the CSP (no inline script, no
81	   external one) leaves the page's own script as the only reader. Under the
82	   cookie it is not stored at all.
83	3. **One QR, the URL.** Nothing generates the JSON any more. The Swift
84	   parser keeps decoding JSON (the visionOS paste field and old pasted
85	   text), so no client breaks.
86	4. **Static paths** are in The signals below.
87	5. **Where the page lives and how it is tested:** `web/`, embedded; the
88	   tests are in The tests.
89	6. **The device record: the name only.** The page sends `device_name` from
90	   its user agent ("Safari on iPhone"); `new_device` already cuts it to 64
91	   characters (`src/core/remote.rs`, `new_device`). No `kind` field.
92	
93	## The record
94	
95	- **`identity.json` gains two additive fields**, `certificate_names:
96	  Vec<String>` and `certificate_expires: Option<SystemTime>`, both
97	  `#[serde(default)]`, so the host knows what the stored certificate
98	  covers without parsing it. `IDENTITY_SCHEMA_VERSION`
99	  (`src/ports/remote.rs:17`) is bumped: **the value in that file at
100	  implementation time, plus one** (it is 1 today; a ticket landing in
101	  parallel may take the next number first). An older file reads with empty
102	  names, which means "reissue at the next bind". `RemoteFiles::load_identity`
103	  (`src/adapters/remote.rs:74`) already refuses a newer file. `model.rs`
104	  and its `SCHEMA_VERSION` (16 today) are untouched; `devices.json` is
105	  unversioned and unchanged.
106	- **Rehydration.** The key stays in the Keychain under
107	  `Identity::key_account`. `bind_remote` (`src/app.rs:2936`) already reads
108	  the key and builds the TLS config; it now first compares the identity's
109	  names and expiry with what this machine answers to (the outward IP from
110	  `local_address()`, `127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, and `<LocalHostName>.local`)
111	  and a 30-day margin. On a miss it reissues over the same key with
112	  `rcgen::KeyPair::from_pem` (as `spki_sha256_of_key` does,
113	  `src/adapters/remote.rs:138-141`), so `spki_sha256` and every pairing are
114	  unchanged (`facts.md`, Settled: the certificate can be reissued over the
115	  same key). It saves `identity.json` through the existing atomic path
116	  directly, as `make_identity` in `app.rs` does at load, then dispatches
117	  `AppAction::CertificateReissued`. It does not go through
118	  `Effect::SaveIdentity`: that arm rebinds when `remote_bound` differs
119	  (`src/app.rs:2895-2898`), and `bind_remote` has just cleared it.
120	- An address that moves after the bind is not covered until the next
121	  bind. The pairing dialog says so when `local_address()` is not in
122	  `certificate_names` and names the fix (turn "Local network" off and on,
123	  which rebinds); the page's warning interstitial is then the one the owner
124	  already knows (Unresolved 7: an address change is another warning).
125	- The page keeps one non-secret marker in `localStorage`: server id, key
126	  hash, device id, name, scope, host name. The token is a second entry
127	  under the default transport.
128	
129	## The signals
130	
131	No new event. The page speaks the existing protocol: `GET info`, `POST
132	pair`, `GET waiting`, `GET projects`, `GET projects/{id}/sessions`, `GET
133	sessions/{id}/last-response` (`screen` for a non-Claude kind), `POST
134	sessions/{id}/send`, `GET ops/{op}`, and the `events` socket with `watch`
135	frames for the content key (`conversation` for `last-response`, `screen`).
136	
137	- **Reads and revisions.** Subscribe first, then snapshot (§4.4). Each
138	  reply carries `epoch` and `revision`; a reply older than what the page
139	  holds for that resource is dropped, a new `epoch` refetches everything,
140	  `resync_required` reconnects and refetches.
141	- **Polling is the floor, the socket the upgrade** (`facts.md`
142	  Unresolved 1; the plan never waits on it). The list and the open
143	  session are refetched every 3 s when no socket is connected and every 30
144	  s when one is (§4.4's visible-view refetch). A socket that fails to
145	  open, or closes, shows "live updates unavailable" and the page carries
146	  on polling; it retries the socket every 30 s. Acceptance step 4 (a
147	  session moves to the top without a reload) therefore holds on either
148	  branch, within 3 s without the socket and at once with it.
149	- **Operation ids.** `crypto.randomUUID()` only when
150	  `window.isSecureContext`, else 16 bytes of `getRandomValues` as hex
151	  (Unresolved 4). A `send` that times out is checked with `GET ops/{op}`,
152	  never resent (§4.5).
153	- **The pairing URL.**
154	  `https://<ip>:<port>/?code=<code>&key=<spki_sha256>&id=<server_id>`, an
155	  IPv6 host in brackets. The host part is the outward IP from
156	  `local_address()`; the `.local` name goes in only if the owner answers
157	  For the owner B favourably, a one-line change in the dialog, since the
158	  certificate already covers both (Unresolved 9). On load the page, before
159	  any request: reads the query, calls `history.replaceState(null, '',
160	  location.pathname)`, then `GET /api/v1/info`, then compares `key` with
161	  `spki_sha256` and `id` with `server_id`, and posts `/pair` only on a
162	  match. On a mismatch it says "this is not the host whose code was
163	  scanned" and sends nothing. With a marker whose server id matches but
164	  whose key differs from `/info`'s, it says "identity changed, pair again"
165	  and sends nothing, token included (§5).
166	- **The code in history.** Unresolved 6 and For the owner C: whether the
167	  browser records the URL before `replaceState` is unknown. The plan
168	  assumes it does. The code is single use and the window closes at the
169	  first pairing, three wrong codes or five minutes (`facts.md`, Settled:
170	  `src/core/remote.rs:46-72`), so a recorded URL is dead after pairing; the
171	  dialog says that. The connection-thread handler never logs a query
172	  (`read_request` has already split it off, `src/adapters/remote.rs:495`)
173	  and `refuse` logs path only (`src/app.rs:3762-3766`).
174	- **Static paths, on the connection thread** (the frame does core state
175	  only, §4.1): `GET /` (`text/html; charset=utf-8`), `GET /app.js`
176	  (`text/javascript; charset=utf-8`), `GET /app.css` (`text/css;
177	  charset=utf-8`). Each answers with `Cache-Control: no-store`,
178	  `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`,
179	  `Connection: close`, and `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none';
180	  script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; base-uri 'none';
181	  form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`. No inline script or style,
182	  no external resource. If a browser's `'self'` does not cover `wss:`, the
183	  socket is blocked and the page is on its polling floor, which it already
184	  handles. Other methods on these paths: 405 with `Allow: GET`. Any other
185	  path outside `/api/v1/` (a `/favicon.ico` included): 404 with the
186	  existing `not_found` body, also on the thread. Paths under `/api/v1/`
187	  go to the frame as today.
188	- **Pool and rate (`facts.md` Unresolved 8).** A static request is
189	  answered with `Connection: close`, so its slot in the pool of four
190	  (`MAX_UNAUTHENTICATED`, `src/adapters/remote.rs:567`) is freed as soon as
191	  the reply is written; a page load is three short requests. Static paths
192	  get their own window, `STATIC_PER_MINUTE = 120` in `Limits`
193	  (`:623-639`), so a reloading browser cannot spend `/pair`'s six a minute
194	  or `/info`'s sixty. Whether an iPhone's parallel connections still
195	  overrun the pool at accept (`:699-706`) needs a device; it is on the
196	  owner's run list, and the plan raises no limit on a guess.
197	- **Without a code and without a token** the page says: "Open the pairing
198	  window on the host (Settings, Remote devices, Allow pairing) and scan
199	  its QR code." No code-entry form: pairing needs the key, which only the
200	  link carries.
201	- **Origin.** Cross-site hijack needs an ambient credential, and the
202	  default transports are not ambient. The host still checks `Origin`
203	  where an ambient one is in play: on the events upgrade, and on any
204	  request authenticated by cookie, `Origin` when present must equal
205	  `https://<Host header>` (the same origin by IP, `.local` name or
206	  loopback alike), else 403 `origin`. Native clients send no `Origin` and
207	  are unaffected.
208	
209	## The actions and effects
210	
211	- `AppAction::CertificateReissued(Identity)`: the core replaces the
212	  stored identity's certificate, names and expiry, keeping `server_id`,
213	  `server_name`, `listen` and `spki_sha256`. It pushes no effect: the file
214	  is already written (above). A core test in `src/core/tests.rs`.
215	- No new `Effect` and no new port method: the reissue uses
216	  `services.remote.save_identity` and `services.secrets.get`, which exist.
217	- **Adapter (`src/adapters/remote.rs`).**
218	  - `RemoteRequest` (`:360`) gains `host`, `origin`, `subprotocols:
219	    Vec<String>` and `cookie_tokens: Vec<String>`. `read_request`
220	    (`:444-514`) fills them: `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` split on commas, a

# Plan: a web control surface on the remote port (#230)

Line numbers are as they are in this worktree at 7fe8949. The facts file
is cited as `facts.md` with its section; "Settled" lines are used as
written, "Unresolved" and "For the owner" lines are named where a decision
rests on one.

The default everywhere below is the design that works whichever way the
open questions are answered: the page pairs and reads over `fetch` with a
bearer header, and treats the events socket as an upgrade it may lose. The
cookie transport and the socket are built, and switch on by a constant
once the owner has run the page on a phone.

## Where this departs from the issue

- **"The one-line excerpt the card shows" does not exist.** The notes and
  `facts.md` (Settled, The tree) say `last_message` is on the session
  record. It is not. It is a field of the hook event
  `EventKind::Stopped { last_message, .. }` (`src/ports/events.rs:24`) and
  the core drops it: `src/core/events.rs:132` matches
  `Stopped { pending, .. }`. `SessionRecord` has no such field and
  `SessionView` (`control/src/lib.rs:637-688`) has none either. So the
  list shows what the wire has: kind, `card` (the card's word), `waiting`
  and `waiting_reason`. The last response appears only in the session view.
  No new read model, no `SessionView` field, no fixture change.
- **"The device's scope in the header" has no source after pairing.** No
  endpoint returns it (`remote_info`, `src/app.rs:3568`, is unauthenticated).
  The page keeps the scope from the `/pair` reply and corrects it when a
  `send` is refused with code `scope` (`src/app.rs:3166-3171`).
- **"Revoked" cannot be told from "never paired" by the code.** Both
  refusals in `authenticate` (`src/app.rs:3127-3152`) are `unauthorized`.
  The page keeps a non-secret marker (server id, key hash, device id, name,
  scope). A 401 with a marker says "this device is no longer paired"; a
  401 without one says "open the pairing window on the host". The host
  adds no code.
- **"Any path outside `/api/v1/` is refused" is true, but late.**
  `serve_remote` does it (`src/app.rs:3023`) after the request took a slot
  in the frame's inbox of 64. The static paths and the 404 for every other
  non-API path are now answered on the connection thread.
- **§5's relay sentence does not hold for a browser.**
  `docs/remote-client.md` §5 says the host's own key check in `/pair` makes
  a relayed request fail. `remote_pair` (`src/app.rs:3636`) compares the
  key in the request body, and under a relay the body comes from the
  impostor's page. The page's `key` check catches a genuine page talking to
  the wrong genuine host (another installation at that address, a rotated
  key). It cannot see the certificate it is on. The spec text is amended
  to say so.
- **`facts.md` says `RemoteReply` is built at about 15 sites.** The tree
  has 11 struct literals: ten in `src/app.rs` (`:1664`, `:1679`, `:2365`,
  `:2371`, `:2376`, `:2754`, `:3570`, `:3723`, `:3736`, `:3767`) and one in
  `src/adapters/remote.rs:829`. No file under `tests/` builds one.
- **An existing test changes.** `tests/ui.rs:7474-7490` parses the copied
  invite as JSON; it becomes a URL.

Decisions the issue asks the plan to settle:

1. **Trust: the click-through is the trust step, said in the dialog; the
   certificate is not offered for download.** A download only helps if the
   device then trusts a manually installed certificate, which needs the
   certificate to meet Apple's rules (`facts.md`, Settled, Apple's TLS
   rules; the tree confirms the current one meets none of SAN, `serverAuth`
   or 825 days: `make_identity`, `src/adapters/remote.rs:102-110`). Whether
   Safari lets the owner proceed at all, and whether the exception then
   covers `fetch` and `wss`, is Unresolved 1 and 2 and For the owner A; the
   plan does not wait on them. It reissues the certificate over the same
   key with the IP and the `.local` name as SANs, `serverAuth` and a
   validity of at most 825 days (Unresolved 1, 2, 3: helps in every
   branch, costs nothing if unneeded). A profile or a download is a later
   issue if A says the click-through is not enough. §5's rule becomes: no
   non-loopback bind serves anything but `/info`, `/pair` and the page's
   three files before pairing; the files are the same bytes for everyone
   and carry no secret.
2. **Token transport: the bearer header on `fetch`, a subprotocol value on
   the socket, the cookie built behind them.** The default needs no browser
   behaviour that `facts.md` leaves open: headers on `fetch` work
   everywhere, and a base64url token is a legal subprotocol token (Settled,
   RFC 6455). The cookie needs Unresolved 5 and For the owner D to be
   favourable, so it is the enhancement (`TRANSPORT` in `app.js`, `'token'`
   by default). The token sits in `localStorage` under the default,
   readable only by this origin's scripts: the CSP (no inline script, no
   external one) leaves the page's own script as the only reader. Under the
   cookie it is not stored at all.
3. **One QR, the URL.** Nothing generates the JSON any more. The Swift
   parser keeps decoding JSON (the visionOS paste field and old pasted
   text), so no client breaks.
4. **Static paths** are in The signals below.
5. **Where the page lives and how it is tested:** `web/`, embedded; the
   tests are in The tests.
6. **The device record: the name only.** The page sends `device_name` from
   its user agent ("Safari on iPhone"); `new_device` already cuts it to 64
   characters (`src/core/remote.rs`, `new_device`). No `kind` field.

## The record

- **`identity.json` gains two additive fields**, `certificate_names:
  Vec<String>` and `certificate_expires: Option<SystemTime>`, both
  `#[serde(default)]`, so the host knows what the stored certificate
  covers without parsing it. `IDENTITY_SCHEMA_VERSION`
  (`src/ports/remote.rs:17`) is bumped: **the value in that file at
  implementation time, plus one** (it is 1 today; a ticket landing in
  parallel may take the next number first). An older file reads with empty
  names, which means "reissue at the next bind". `RemoteFiles::load_identity`
  (`src/adapters/remote.rs:74`) already refuses a newer file. `model.rs`
  and its `SCHEMA_VERSION` (16 today) are untouched; `devices.json` is
  unversioned and unchanged.
- **Rehydration.** The key stays in the Keychain under
  `Identity::key_account`. `bind_remote` (`src/app.rs:2936`) already reads
  the key and builds the TLS config; it now first compares the identity's
  names and expiry with what this machine answers to (the outward IP from
  `local_address()`, `127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, and `<LocalHostName>.local`)
  and a 30-day margin. On a miss it reissues over the same key with
  `rcgen::KeyPair::from_pem` (as `spki_sha256_of_key` does,
  `src/adapters/remote.rs:138-141`), so `spki_sha256` and every pairing are
  unchanged (`facts.md`, Settled: the certificate can be reissued over the
  same key). It saves `identity.json` through the existing atomic path
  directly, as `make_identity` in `app.rs` does at load, then dispatches
  `AppAction::CertificateReissued`. It does not go through
  `Effect::SaveIdentity`: that arm rebinds when `remote_bound` differs
  (`src/app.rs:2895-2898`), and `bind_remote` has just cleared it.
- An address that moves after the bind is not covered until the next
  bind. The pairing dialog says so when `local_address()` is not in
  `certificate_names` and names the fix (turn "Local network" off and on,
  which rebinds); the page's warning interstitial is then the one the owner
  already knows (Unresolved 7: an address change is another warning).
- The page keeps one non-secret marker in `localStorage`: server id, key
  hash, device id, name, scope, host name. The token is a second entry
  under the default transport.

## The signals

No new event. The page speaks the existing protocol: `GET info`, `POST
pair`, `GET waiting`, `GET projects`, `GET projects/{id}/sessions`, `GET
sessions/{id}/last-response` (`screen` for a non-Claude kind), `POST
sessions/{id}/send`, `GET ops/{op}`, and the `events` socket with `watch`
frames for the content key (`conversation` for `last-response`, `screen`).

- **Reads and revisions.** Subscribe first, then snapshot (§4.4). Each
  reply carries `epoch` and `revision`; a reply older than what the page
  holds for that resource is dropped, a new `epoch` refetches everything,
  `resync_required` reconnects and refetches.
- **Polling is the floor, the socket the upgrade** (`facts.md`
  Unresolved 1; the plan never waits on it). The list and the open
  session are refetched every 3 s when no socket is connected and every 30
  s when one is (§4.4's visible-view refetch). A socket that fails to
  open, or closes, shows "live updates unavailable" and the page carries
  on polling; it retries the socket every 30 s. Acceptance step 4 (a
  session moves to the top without a reload) therefore holds on either
  branch, within 3 s without the socket and at once with it.
- **Operation ids.** `crypto.randomUUID()` only when
  `window.isSecureContext`, else 16 bytes of `getRandomValues` as hex
  (Unresolved 4). A `send` that times out is checked with `GET ops/{op}`,
  never resent (§4.5).
- **The pairing URL.**
  `https://<ip>:<port>/?code=<code>&key=<spki_sha256>&id=<server_id>`, an
  IPv6 host in brackets. The host part is the outward IP from
  `local_address()`; the `.local` name goes in only if the owner answers
  For the owner B favourably, a one-line change in the dialog, since the
  certificate already covers both (Unresolved 9). On load the page, before
  any request: reads the query, calls `history.replaceState(null, '',
  location.pathname)`, then `GET /api/v1/info`, then compares `key` with
  `spki_sha256` and `id` with `server_id`, and posts `/pair` only on a
  match. On a mismatch it says "this is not the host whose code was
  scanned" and sends nothing. With a marker whose server id matches but
  whose key differs from `/info`'s, it says "identity changed, pair again"
  and sends nothing, token included (§5).
- **The code in history.** Unresolved 6 and For the owner C: whether the
  browser records the URL before `replaceState` is unknown. The plan
  assumes it does. The code is single use and the window closes at the
  first pairing, three wrong codes or five minutes (`facts.md`, Settled:
  `src/core/remote.rs:46-72`), so a recorded URL is dead after pairing; the
  dialog says that. The connection-thread handler never logs a query
  (`read_request` has already split it off, `src/adapters/remote.rs:495`)
  and `refuse` logs path only (`src/app.rs:3762-3766`).
- **Static paths, on the connection thread** (the frame does core state
  only, §4.1): `GET /` (`text/html; charset=utf-8`), `GET /app.js`
  (`text/javascript; charset=utf-8`), `GET /app.css` (`text/css;
  charset=utf-8`). Each answers with `Cache-Control: no-store`,
  `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`,
  `Connection: close`, and `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none';
  script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; base-uri 'none';
  form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`. No inline script or style,
  no external resource. If a browser's `'self'` does not cover `wss:`, the
  socket is blocked and the page is on its polling floor, which it already
  handles. Other methods on these paths: 405 with `Allow: GET`. Any other
  path outside `/api/v1/` (a `/favicon.ico` included): 404 with the
  existing `not_found` body, also on the thread. Paths under `/api/v1/`
  go to the frame as today.
- **Pool and rate (`facts.md` Unresolved 8).** A static request is
  answered with `Connection: close`, so its slot in the pool of four
  (`MAX_UNAUTHENTICATED`, `src/adapters/remote.rs:567`) is freed as soon as
  the reply is written; a page load is three short requests. Static paths
  get their own window, `STATIC_PER_MINUTE = 120` in `Limits`
  (`:623-639`), so a reloading browser cannot spend `/pair`'s six a minute
  or `/info`'s sixty. Whether an iPhone's parallel connections still
  overrun the pool at accept (`:699-706`) needs a device; it is on the
  owner's run list, and the plan raises no limit on a guess.
- **Without a code and without a token** the page says: "Open the pairing
  window on the host (Settings, Remote devices, Allow pairing) and scan
  its QR code." No code-entry form: pairing needs the key, which only the
  link carries.
- **Origin.** Cross-site hijack needs an ambient credential, and the
  default transports are not ambient. The host still checks `Origin`
  where an ambient one is in play: on the events upgrade, and on any
  request authenticated by cookie, `Origin` when present must equal
  `https://<Host header>` (the same origin by IP, `.local` name or
  loopback alike), else 403 `origin`. Native clients send no `Origin` and
  are unaffected.

## The actions and effects

- `AppAction::CertificateReissued(Identity)`: the core replaces the
  stored identity's certificate, names and expiry, keeping `server_id`,
  `server_name`, `listen` and `spki_sha256`. It pushes no effect: the file
  is already written (above). A core test in `src/core/tests.rs`.
- No new `Effect` and no new port method: the reissue uses
  `services.remote.save_identity` and `services.secrets.get`, which exist.
- **Adapter (`src/adapters/remote.rs`).**
  - `RemoteRequest` (`:360`) gains `host`, `origin`, `subprotocols:
    Vec<String>` and `cookie_tokens: Vec<String>`. `read_request`
    (`:444-514`) fills them: `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` split on commas, a
    `bearer.<token>` entry taken as the token when no `Authorization`
    header is present, and every cookie named `sb_*` collected (the rest of
    the `Cookie` header is dropped, never stored or logged, since cookies
    are shared across ports on a host, RFC 6265 per `facts.md`). Only the
    adapter builds `RemoteRequest` (`facts.md`, Settled), so nothing else
    changes. It is not in `ports/` or `model.rs`, so CLAUDE.md's additivity
    rule does not name it; the additions are additive anyway.
  - `RemoteReply` (`:389`) gains `headers: Vec<(String, String)>` and a
    constructor `RemoteReply::new(status, body, authenticated)`; the 11
    literals above call it. Only `/pair` sets a header (`Set-Cookie`).
  - `respond` (`:530`) takes extra headers; a new `respond_static` writes
    the three files. `respond_upgrade` (`:519`) echoes
    `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: switchboard.v1` when the request offered it
    (RFC 6455: the client fails on a subprotocol it did not offer, and the
    server never echoes the token entry; `facts.md`, Settled). A native
    client offers none and gets none.
  - `connection` (`:770`) answers static and non-API paths before the
    frame, after the rate check.
  - `make_identity` (`:95`) and a new `reissue_certificate(identity, key_pem,
    names, now)` share one certificate builder: SANs, `serverAuth`,
    `not_after` = now + 825 days minus a day. `time` may need to become a
    direct dependency for `OffsetDateTime`; check whether `rcgen` re-exports
    it. `certificate_names()` and `invite_url(ip, port, code, key,
    server_id)` are pure functions beside `local_address()` (`:962`).
- **Router (`src/app.rs`).**
  - `authenticate` (`:3127`) reads `request.bearer`, then
    `cookie_tokens`, and applies the origin rule for the cookie case.
  - `remote_subscribe` (`:2723`) applies the origin rule.
  - `remote_pair` (`:3606`) honours an optional `"cookie": true` in the
    body: the reply keeps the token in the body (native clients read it) and
    adds `Set-Cookie: sb_<first 8 hex of server_id>=<token>; HttpOnly;
    Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/api/v1/; Max-Age=31536000`. The name
    carries the server id so two instances on one Mac do not clash.
  - `bind_remote` (`:2936`) reissues first.
  - The `/api/v1/` prefix arm (`:3023`) stays as the backstop.
- **New files:** `web/index.html`, `web/app.js`, `web/app.css`, and
  `src/adapters/web.rs` (`include_str!("../../web/...")`, one lookup
  function from method and path to a file, and the header set). No build
  step, no dependency for the page.

## The UI

- **The page** (`web/`): the header shows the host name and the device's
  scope; sessions are grouped by project, waiting ones first and marked,
  each row with its kind, `card` word and `waiting_reason` (`hide_workers`
  already applies, `src/app.rs:2687`); a session view shows the last
  response (Claude Code) or the screen (anything else), refreshed per The
  signals; a reply box posts `send` when the scope is `control` and is
  hidden otherwise. Plain statements for "identity changed, pair again",
  "this device is no longer paired", "live updates unavailable". A
  `prompt_refusal` or `trust_question` session shows its reason and no
  reply box; resume and the trust answer are not in this cut.
- **The pairing window** (`src/ui/remote.rs:155-206`): the QR and "Copy
  invite" carry the URL, the `json!` call at `:160-166` is replaced by
  `remote::invite_url`, and the address label shows the URL's host and
  port. Under it, three sentences: a browser shows a certificate warning
  once, and accepting it on the local network is the trust step (the page
  compares the key but cannot see the certificate it is on); the link holds
  the code, which works once and for five minutes, so a copy left in the
  browser's history is dead after pairing; the certificate is renewed over
  the same key, so a renewal does not unpair anyone. When
  `local_address()` is not in `certificate_names` it adds the restart note.
- **The paired-devices list** (`:230-275`) needs no change: a browser is a
  row with a scope selector and Revoke, and revoking closes its socket
  (existing test `revoke_closes_the_devices_socket`, `tests/remote.rs:2892`).
- **Swift text path:** `PairingInvite.parse`
  (`client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift:93-116`) tries a URL first
  (`URLComponents`: host and port into `addresses`, `code`, `key`, `id`)
  and JSON second, so `main.swift:111`, `BrowserView.swift:106,883` and
  every `PairingInvite(...)` call (`facts.md`, Settled: it is built as a list
  of one) work unchanged. The CLI usage string (`main.swift:13`) and the
  README's "Copy invite" text say the QR holds a URL.

## The tests

Rust (the commands in CLAUDE.md; Linux CI runs them):

- `src/adapters/remote.rs` unit tests: a reissued certificate keeps
  `spki_sha256` (`spki_sha256_of_cert` equals the key's hash); its DER
  holds the SAN names and the `serverAuth` OID; `certificate_expires` is at
  most 825 days out; reissue is skipped when names and margin are met;
  `invite_url` for IPv4 and a bracketed IPv6 host; `read_request` takes
  the three token transports and drops other cookies.
- `src/core/tests.rs`: `CertificateReissued` replaces certificate fields
  and keeps `spki_sha256`, `server_id` and `listen`, and returns no
  effect.
- `tests/remote.rs`: extend `http` (`:245`) to return headers (a thin
  wrapper keeps current callers). Then: the three paths answer with the
  headers named above; a path with `?code=` answers the page and reaches no
  frame; other methods get 405; `/favicon.ico` gets 404 without a frame
  pass; the static window answers 429 past 120; four sequential static
  loads leave the pool free (model: `stalled_strangers_fill_their_own_pool_and_never_a_paired_clients`,
  `:3226`); the embedded `index.html` names only `/app.js` and `/app.css`,
  has no inline script and no `http` URL, and every `/api/v1/...` literal
  in `app.js` is an endpoint the host serves. The pairing flow as the page
  does it, with the host's own client as the CLI does: `/info`, key
  compare, `/pair` with a browser-style `device_name`, a read with the
  bearer header; a socket upgrade offering `switchboard.v1, bearer.<token>`
  gets 101 echoing `switchboard.v1` and not the token (extend
  `subscribe_at`, `:1960`); `/pair` with `"cookie": true` sets the cookie
  with `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict`, a cookie-authenticated read
  works, a cookie-authenticated request with a foreign `Origin` gets 403,
  a bearer request with a foreign `Origin` is unaffected; after
  `RevokeDevice` the next request is `unauthorized` and the socket closes.
  `pair_is_rate_limited_per_listener` (`:1406`) and
  `the_allowlist_refuses_everything_else_with_no_side_effect` (`:682`) stay
  as they are and still pass.
- `tests/ui.rs:7474`: the copied invite is a URL with `code`, `key` and
  `id` equal to the window's code, the identity's key hash and server id;
  the dialog shows the trust sentences.
- No fixture change: no view or wire body changes. The Swift fixtures stay
  as they are.

Swift (`client/`, run as `client/README.md` says; not run by CI on
Linux): `FixturesTests.swift:156` gets URL cases beside the JSON one, an
IPv6 host, and a URL with an unknown query key.

The page's own logic (query parse, `replaceState`, reconcile) has no
runner and the issue rules out a JS dependency, so it is checked by the
manual run below, and the embedded-page test above is the guard against
the page naming a path the host does not serve.

Manual acceptance, against a test data dir and tmux socket
(`SWITCHBOARD_DATA_DIR`, `SWITCHBOARD_TMUX_SOCKET`, script lines
`remote-listen lan <port>` and `pairing <code>`): open the window, scan
the QR with a phone, accept the warning, see the sessions; start a session
waiting with `switchboard-hook PermissionRequest` and watch it move to the
top without a reload (within 3 s if the socket is unavailable); send a
reply from the phone with `control` scope and watch it arrive; revoke the
phone in the dialog and the page says so on its next request. None of
these steps depends on the socket, the cookie or the `.local` name. The
owner's run also answers For the owner A through D, recorded in the design
status section: whether the page loads after the warning, whether `wss`
connects, whether `.local` resolves, whether the cookie works. A, B and D
each flip one constant (`TRANSPORT`, the host in the URL) and add no code.

## Docs, in the same commit

- `docs/remote-client.md`: §4.1 gets the static-file bullet and the
  thread it runs on; §4.3 lists the three paths; §5 changes "Require
  pairing before anything but `/info` and `/pair`" to add the page's files,
  the QR line to the URL, the token line to the three transports, and the
  relay sentence as in the departures; the certificate line gets the SANs,
  `serverAuth` and the 825-day bound, with the pin unchanged by a reissue.
- `docs/design.md`: a "Web control surface" item in the Remote client
  section (starts `## Remote client (2026-10-12)`, `docs/design.md:3107`),
  with the Known gaps at the end of that section (`:3573`) extended: no
  excerpt on rows, scope stale until a refused send, no certificate
  download or profile, no JS tests, an address change needs a rebind,
  Unresolved 1 through 9 and A through D as open until the phone run.
- `README.md`: Layout rows for `src/adapters/web.rs` and `web/*`; the
  `SWITCHBOARD_REMOTE_PORT` paragraph's "Copy invite" text now says URL, and
  that opening it in a browser pairs it; the data directory entry for
  `identity.json` mentions the certificate names.
- `CHANGELOG.md`, under Unreleased: "The remote port serves a web page:
  open the pairing window's QR code on a phone or any browser on the local
  network to see the sessions, which are waiting, and reply."

## Order inside the one commit (the app builds and runs after each)

1. `web/`, `src/adapters/web.rs`, the connection-thread static answers,
   the static window, `RemoteReply::new`, the extended `http` helper.
2. The `RemoteRequest` fields, the three token transports, the subprotocol
   echo, the origin rule, the cookie on `/pair`.
3. The certificate builder, `reissue_certificate`, the two `Identity`
   fields and the version bump, `CertificateReissued`, the `bind_remote`
   call.
4. `invite_url`, the dialog, the Swift parser.
5. The tests and docs above; `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy --locked
   --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked
   --workspace`.

## Commit message

Serve a browser page from the remote port, paired from a URL in the pairing QR

## Contract additions (for the commit message body)

- `AppAction::CertificateReissued(Identity)` in `src/core/action.rs`; no
  new `Effect`, no new port method.
- `Identity.certificate_names: Vec<String>` and
  `Identity.certificate_expires: Option<SystemTime>` (`#[serde(default)]`)
  in `src/ports/remote.rs`; `IDENTITY_SCHEMA_VERSION` set to the value in
  that file at implementation time, plus one. No change to `model.rs` or
  `SCHEMA_VERSION`; `devices.json` unchanged.
- `RemoteRequest` fields `host`, `origin`, `subprotocols`, `cookie_tokens`;
  `RemoteReply.headers` and `RemoteReply::new` (both in
  `src/adapters/remote.rs`, outside the shared contract).
- `/pair` body: optional `cookie` (bool). `/pair` reply: optional
  `Set-Cookie`, the body unchanged.
- Events upgrade: a `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` of `switchboard.v1` is echoed;
  `bearer.<token>` is accepted as a token carrier. Refusal code `origin`
  (403) for a cookie-authenticated request or an upgrade whose `Origin` is
  not the host's own.
- Served paths: `GET /`, `/app.js`, `/app.css`; every other non-API path
  is 404 on the connection thread.
- New files `src/adapters/web.rs`, `web/index.html`, `web/app.js`,
  `web/app.css`; new pure functions `remote::invite_url`,
  `remote::certificate_names`, `remote::reissue_certificate`.
- Swift: `PairingInvite.parse` accepts a URL as well as JSON; no new type
  and no changed initializer.
- Wire bodies, `control/`, and the shared fixtures: no change.
